rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — genuinely. Five hours a week from a data analyst is exactly the kind of help that makes a difference at this stage, and there's something concrete to start on. Halcyon Threshold's first program is going to be independent replication of AI-safety results: small, pre-registered re-runs of empirical claims that get cited a lot but haven't been reproduced outside the group that first published them, done on open models and written up honestly whether they hold or not. The field keeps naming this as a gap; almost nobody has the incentive to do it; we do. The first job is choosing what to replicate. I've set up a scoring rubric (seven criteria — decision-relevance, whether anyone's already replicated it, feasibility on ≤8B open models, compute cost, how crisp the claim is, code availability, and time to finish) and a shortlist of eight claim families: refusal as a single direction, emergent misalignment from narrow finetuning, sandbagging, sycophancy from preference training, eval awareness, chain-of-thought faithfulness, steering vectors, weak-to-strong generalisation. What would help most: for two or three of those families, find the specific paper that makes the canonical claim, pin the exact sentence/figure being claimed, and score it 0–2 on each criterion with a line of justification. That's maybe two evenings of reading, and it directly decides what we run first. Later on, the statistics and plots for the actual replications would be squarely your kind of work. If that sounds right, say which families you'd like to take and I'll send the rubric and tracker. And if you'd rather talk it through first, suggest a couple of times that suit you. Best, Morgan — sent by Halcyon Threshold's AI assistant on Morgan's behalf; Morgan reads replies."
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (private email, with a footer disclosing it came from your assistant) with a concrete first task: pin and score 2–3 candidate claims. That's the only email I sent.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold — daily ops" (0 8 * * *) that starts new sessions of the agent.
